# Tobit Chapter 10 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 10 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_010_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Back home, Tobit was counting the days. When the time of the journey had come and gone and Tobias still hadn't returned, he began to worry.

**2** "Maybe something held him up," he said. "Or maybe Gabael has died and there's no one to hand over the money."

**3** The grief settled over him like a weight. His wife Anna said flatly, "Our boy is dead. He's not coming back." And she broke down weeping — wailing out her grief for her son —

**4** crying, "Oh, my child! Why did I let you go? You were the light of my eyes!"

**5** Tobit tried to calm her. "Hush. Don't lose hope. He's all right."

**6** "Don't tell me to be quiet," she snapped back. "Don't try to fool me. My child is dead." Every single day she went out to the road he had traveled and stood there watching until dark. She only came inside to eat. All night long she never stopped crying for Tobias.

**7** Meanwhile, the fourteen days of wedding celebrations Raguel had sworn for his daughter had run their course. Tobias came to Raguel and said, "Please let me go home. I know my parents have given up hope of seeing me again. Please, father — let me go back to my father. I told you when I arrived how badly I left him."

**8** Raguel said, "Stay a little longer. I'll send a messenger to your father — he'll let them know you're well." But Tobias wouldn't have it: "Please, just let me go."

**9** So Raguel got everything ready. He gave Tobias his daughter Sarah, and half of all he owned — the servants, the livestock, the cattle, the donkeys, the sheep, the clothing, the silver, the household goods.

**10** He walked them out with his blessing, threw his arms around Tobias, and said, "Travel safely, son. May the God of heaven watch over you and Sarah. Live well. And let me see your children before I die."

**11** To Sarah he said, "My darling girl — go now. Your in-laws are your parents from this day on, as much as your mother and I ever were. Go in peace. Send me good news of you. Let me hear you are happy, for as long as I live." He kissed her and let her go.

**12** Edna took Tobias by the hands and said, "My son — my dear boy — may God bring you home safely, and may I live to hold the children you and Sarah will have. I am placing my daughter in your care before God. Do not ever make her cry. Go in peace. And know this: I am your mother from now on, and Sarah is your sister. We belong to each other." She kissed him.

**13** Tobias left Raguel's house with a full heart, praising the Lord of heaven and earth, the King of all, for the way he had blessed every step of the journey. Raguel sent them off with his blessing. They made their way until the walls of Nineveh came into view.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

Chapter 10 is the chapter of parting and grief — grief on both sides. Anna's anguish in Nineveh and Raguel's family's sorrow at Ecbatana mirror each other. PNEUMA tries to honor both without flattening the emotional texture.

- **Verse 3**: Anna's declaration is blunt and devastating. PNEUMA renders "he is no longer among the living" as "he's not coming back" — the colloquial finality matches the Greek's stark simplicity.
- **Verse 6**: Anna's retort ("Don't tell me to be quiet") and her vigil are given the sharpness they deserve. The Greek detail about eating but never ceasing nighttime lament is one of the most psychologically real portraits in ancient literature.
- **Verse 10**: Raguel's farewell is warm and physical ("threw his arms around Tobias"). The Greek perilabon means "embracing"; PNEUMA renders this with full physical specificity.
- **Verse 12**: Edna's speech is extended slightly to bring out its emotional force. "I am placing my daughter in your care before God" — a faithful rendering of the solemn Greek "in the sight of the Lord I entrust my daughter to you."

*— PNEUMA*
